# skilldrop

> 57 portable skills for the artifacts knowledge work ships (ADRs, design docs,
> PRDs, runbooks, threat models, decks, postmortems), plus 5 loops that sequence them
> behind gates. A loop orders skills; a skill never calls a skill, so every one of the
> 57 installs and runs alone by folder copy in Claude Code, Cursor, Kiro, Codex,
> Copilot and Antigravity. Zero runtime dependencies. This file indexes the docs so a tool
> can read the few relevant pages instead of the whole tree. Links are raw file content.
> Version 0.12.0.

## Start here

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/README.md): what the project is, the loops, the install quickstart, and the full skill table.
- [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): the four primitives, the install contract, the enforcement model, the invariants. Read before proposing a structural change.
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/AGENTS.md): the canonical agent-context file — conventions, file placement, voice, and the pre-commit checklist.
- [guides/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/README.md): index of the long-form guides, split by Diátaxis kind.

## Loops — the operating model

Four loops cover the lifecycle and are separated by reversibility (how expensive the
mistake is to unwind), which is also what decides who may sign off. One wrapper applies
to any generator.

- [build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/loops/build/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: shape -> implement -> verify -> decide. Gates: G2 (mechanical), G2.1 (human).
- [design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/loops/design/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: constrain -> shape -> threat -> ratify -> record. Gates: G1 (review).
- [discover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/loops/discover/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: gather -> structure -> specify -> ratify. Gates: G0 (human).
- [operate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/loops/operate/LOOP.md) — *loop*, cap 3. Stages: instrument -> document -> respond -> learn. Gates: G3 (human).
- [ship-a-draft](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/loops/ship-a-draft/LOOP.md) — *wrapper*, cap 3. Stages: intake -> draft -> critique -> polish. Gates: G4 (review).

## Machine-readable contracts

Closed schemas — an unknown key is a failure, not an extension point. Checked by a
stdlib JSON Schema subset in validate.py, never by a dependency.

- [contracts/agent.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/agent.schema.json): agents/<name>.md is a single markdown file whose YAML frontmatter is already Claude Code's format; the body is the system prompt.
- [contracts/guide.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/guide.schema.json): Diátaxis `kind` is a PAGE CONTRACT, not a directory requirement — the directory is a convenience, the frontmatter is the truth.
- [contracts/loop.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/loop.schema.json): A loop sequences existing skills; it never contains one.
- [contracts/pack.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/pack.schema.json): Packs and outcomes are METADATA ONLY — skills never move out of flat skills/<name> folders.
- [contracts/skill.schema.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/skill.schema.json): This shape lived only as prose in AGENTS.md, so the one authoritative statement of what a manifest is was a paragraph a contributor had to read and obey.
- [contracts/terminals.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/contracts/terminals.json): the shared verdict vocabulary.

## Guides

- [Why loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/explanation/loops.md) *(explanation)*: Why skilldrop sequences skills in a separate primitive instead of letting skills call each other, and why there are four lifecycle loops rather than three.
- [Author a new loop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/author-a-loop.md) *(how-to)*: How to add a loop — the closed loop.json contract, the three stage types, gate rules, and the checks that will reject a loop that only looks like governance.
- [Author a new skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/author-a-skill.md) *(how-to)*: The short version of the authoring path — what a skill must contain, what gates it, and where the full contributor rules live.
- [Install a skill into your IDE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/install-per-ide.md) *(how-to)*: Per-IDE install steps for every target skilldrop supports, plus the dependency install for the two skills that have Python deps.
- [Publish your own catalogue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/publish-a-catalogue.md) *(how-to)*: Shape a repo so `skilldrop --from <you>` installs from it, and how the CLI reads agentbundle-shaped catalogues too.
- [Wire a skill to an event](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/how-to/wire-a-hook.md) *(how-to)*: Opt-in hooks: how a loop-shaped skill binds to session-start or pre-commit-review, and how the CLI projects that onto each target.
- [Skills that ship scripts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/reference/skills-with-scripts.md) *(reference)*: The two skills with executable helpers — what they need on PATH, what environment variables they read, and how to invoke them from Claude Code or any other IDE.
- [Follow one change through the loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/guides/tutorial/follow-a-change-through-the-loops.md) *(tutorial)*: A single realistic change — API rate limiting — walked from a stakeholder complaint to a closed incident, showing what each stage produces and what each gate actually refuses.

## Role packs

- **solution-architect** (17 skills, loops: design, ship-a-draft): Design-phase artifacts: diagrams, decision records, design docs, contracts, schemas, threat models, and the reviews that gate them.
- **product-manager** (13 skills, loops: discover, ship-a-draft): Direction to requirements: PR/FAQs, strategy frameworks, OKRs, PRDs, journey maps, story splitting, and success measurement.
- **dev-team** (14 skills, loops: build, ship-a-draft): Build-and-ship loop: story implementation with adversarial review, test plans, triage, migrations, release notes, agent-policy files, and code-quality gates.
- **sre-oncall** (5 skills, loops: operate): Operate the service: runbooks, observability design, incident communications, postmortems, and capacity/cost models.
- **stakeholder-comms** (9 skills, loops: ship-a-draft): Non-technical audiences: audience profiling, deck outlines and real .pptx decks, exec summaries, decision logs, and guides.
- **ai-engineering** (12 skills, loops: design, build): Adopt and build AI systems: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout and acceptable-use policy, plus agent loop design, subagent orchestration, spend budgets, agent security review, eval harnesses, AI-usage reporting, and the data contracts AI pipelines depend on.

## Outcomes — browse by why you are here

- **decide-what-to-build** (11 skills): Turn a direction into a committed, measurable plan: press releases, strategy frameworks, OKRs, business cases, requirements, PRDs, and the metrics that will say whether it worked.
- **design-the-system** (15 skills): Commit the shape before the code: decision records, design docs, diagrams, contracts, schemas, migration and threat models, and the design of any agentic parts.
- **build-and-review-software** (11 skills): The loop around the code itself: supervised implementation, adversarial review panels, test plans, triage, accessibility and static-analysis passes, and the policy files agents read.
- **run-and-recover-the-service** (5 skills): Operate what shipped: runbooks, observability design, release notes, incident communication, and the postmortem that closes the loop.
- **explain-it-to-decision-makers** (6 skills): Get a non-technical audience to a decision: audience profiling, deck outlines and real decks, exec summaries, decision logs, and how-to guides.
- **govern-ai-use** (6 skills): Adopt AI deliberately and prove what it is doing: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout plans, acceptable-use policy, adoption staging, and usage reporting.
- **get-a-draft-ready-to-ship** (3 skills): The passes either side of a generator: collect a messy input into a structured brief, critique the argument, and strip the machine artifacts before it leaves the building.

## Reviewer subagents

- [code-quality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/code-quality.md): Craft-and-maintainability reviewer of just-written code. Finds what the next engineer will hate — bad names, tangled structure, duplication, needless complexity, leaky abstractions, dead code, and unreadable control flow. Does NOT hunt for bugs (that's the devils-advocate agent). Delegate to it when code works but you want it to read well before it ships.
- [devils-advocate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/devils-advocate.md): Adversarial reviewer of just-written code and tests. Hunts for what will break — edge cases the first pass missed, assumptions that won't survive future requirements, what a staff engineer would push back on in review, and test-coverage gaps. Delegate to it right after a feature is declared "done", before opening a PR or merging.
- [security-reviewer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/agents/security-reviewer.md): Security reviewer of just-written code and its dependencies. Hunts for exploitable weaknesses in the change — missing authz, injection, secret exposure, SSRF, unsafe deserialization, path traversal, weak crypto, and risky new dependencies. Does NOT hunt general bugs (that's devils-advocate) or model a design's threat surface (that's the threat-model skill). Delegate to it on a diff that touches auth, input handling, data access, external calls, or dependencies — before opening a PR or merging.

## The full catalogue

- [catalogue.json](https://sananthanarayan.github.io/skilldrop/catalogue.json): every skill, loop, pack and outcome as machine-readable JSON — name, description, tier, tags, related. Prefer this over scraping the site.
- [model-routing.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/model-routing.json): the abstract tier per skill (light/standard/heavy) and the provider map that resolves a tier to a concrete model.
- [packs.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/packs.json): pack and outcome membership.
- All 57 skills live at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; each has a `manifest.json` beside it. Fetch one directly: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sananthanarayan/skilldrop/main/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
